issue.title: [ML] Support date_nanos time field

repository.name: kibana
repository.description: Your window into all of your data

issue.body:
Support for the `date_nanos` was added to Kibana in 7.3.0 (see https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/36111), however various parts of the ML UI do not currently work when the time field of the Elasticsearch index is mapped as type `date_nanos`.

This meta issue tracks the functionality that needs fixing to support `date_nanos` type date fields:

- [x] Validation in the job wizards fails, preventing the job being created (https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/52921)
- [x] 'Use full time range' button fails in the job wizards; page goes blank with an invalid bounds error in the browser console _(no longer found in 7.7)_
- [x] 'Use full time range' button fails in the Data Visualizer; page goes blank with a TypeError in the browser console _(no longer found in 7.7)_
- [x] Datafeed preview fails in the advanced job wizard, with an error of the form `[illegal_argument_exception] date[+49916826-11-21T00:53:20Z] is after 2262-04-11T23:47:16.854775807 and cannot be stored in nanosecond resolution"` _(no longer found in 7.7)_
- [x] Transforms using a group_by on a date_histogram of the `date_nanos` field fail with  `BulkIndexingException` seen in job messages _(no longer found in 7.7)_
- [x] The preview table in the Transforms wizard show a blank column for the aggregation - caused by https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/53168. Fixed in https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/61792

issue.title: Fix date_nanos in composite aggs

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
It looks like `date_nanos` fields weren't likely to work properly in
composite aggs because composites iterate field values using points and
we weren't converting the points into milliseconds. Because the doc
values were coming back in milliseconds we ended up geting very confused
and just never collecting sub-aggregations.

This fixes that by adding a method to `DateFieldMapper.Resolution` to
`parsePointAsMillis` which is similarly in name and function to
`NumberFieldMapper.NumberType`'s `parsePoint` except that it normalizes
to milliseconds which is what aggs need at the moment.

Closes #53168
